title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for alcohol use.

Vitals: BP 138/84, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, weight loss.
HEENT: Negative for vision changes.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or abdominal pain.
Neurological: Negative for tremors or dizziness.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

HPI: Copied Forward: Patient is an 89-year-old female presenting for ongoing management of alcohol use. She reports consistent consumption.
Update: The patient reports she is currently drinking and continues to consume alcohol daily. She expresses a desire to manage her intake but admits difficulty with consistency. She denies any new acute physical symptoms.

Medication List:
- Multivitamin daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears well-nourished.
Psychiatric: Cooperative, normal mood, congruent affect.
Skin: No significant lesions or rashes.

Assessment:
1. Alcohol use disorder, moderate.

Plan:
1. Discussed the risks associated with alcohol use disorder, moderate.
2. Encouraged the patient to reduce daily consumption.
3. Will follow up in four weeks to monitor progress.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, moderate or severe, indexes to alcohol dependence: F10.20 (HCC 139).

distractors.why: Moderate or severe use disorder is dependence (F10.2-); abuse has no HCC.
A use disorder with a severity is documented.

hccs.label: Alcohol Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Alcohol Use with Specified Non-Psychotic Complications
